motivation: MS-147 addendum: hokkaido normal pairs keep z>=2 at .308 (other regions .025-.037) even when both acquisitions are token-SCL clean, so the residual over-dispersion is not cloud. Hypothesis: it is seasonal surface change (snow / crop cycle) that a gap x season table fitted on three warm regions (LOEO) cannot represent.
question: Does an in-region seasonal baseline (table fitted on the SAME region's held-out tiles) bring hokkaido's normal z>=2 rate down to the level of the other regions without destroying event detection?
data: arrival_v0/<region>/single_fp16 + meta (base). NORMAL pair = consecutive clear>=.5 acquisitions not crossing post_index (as change_calibration v0.1). EVENT pair = last clear pre / first clear post on positive tiles, token mask >=.25 (as token calibration v0.2).
split: tiles of the target region split by hash parity into fit-half A and eval-half B (tile-disjoint). Tables are fitted on A, all rates evaluated on B only.

arms.loeo: gap x season(DJF/MAM/JJA/SON) table from the other three regions (reference = current pipeline)
arms.inregion_season: gap x season table fitted on half A of the target region
arms.inregion_month: gap x month table fitted on half A (finer season axis; cells with <2000 tokens fall back to season cell)

metrics: normal_z2: fraction of normal-pair tokens (subsample .25) with z>=2 on half B
event_auc: pooled token AUC mask vs non-mask on event pairs of half B

gate.pass: for hokkaido, inregion_season or inregion_month has normal_z2 <= .10 AND event_auc >= loeo event_auc - .03 (and >= .75)
gate.control: for the other three regions, in-region normal_z2 must not exceed loeo by more than .02 (in-region fitting should not hurt where LOEO already works)
gate.fail_reading: if normal_z2 stays > .15 with in-region tables, hokkaido over-dispersion is tile-specific (not seasonal) and a per-tile baseline (time-series of the same tile) is the next candidate; if event_auc collapses, the seasonal table absorbs the event signal (event confounded with season) and the result is a benchmark caveat, not a fix

compute: GPU0 or CPU, minutes; no training
allowed_claims_after: a seasonal baseline row in the reliability track table; no downstream reader claim
not_allowed: changing the gate after seeing results; using half B for fitting
